I am a woman of forty years, and I farm this small sorghum plot near my home. It is only a small piece of land, so I cannot spend much on it — the bigger plots take most of what I can buy from the cooperative. I will use the seed I saved from last year's harvest, like my mother did, and put what manure I can carry from our animals. For sorghum the rains usually carry it, by God's grace.

I asked my husband and we agreed: a small bit of DAP at planting if the cooperative brings it in time, but no top-dressing of urea — that we save for the teff and the bigger plot. No chemicals for spraying, we have never used them on sorghum. The work I will do myself with help from my older children when school allows.
